newsitem.title: UK: IPE natural gas futures mixed, focus on winter.
newsitem.headline: IPE natural gas futures mixed, focus on winter.

text.p: IPE natural gas failed to head in a single direction on Friday morning, with January and February making gains in the face of losses in other months.
Little interest was seen for the prompt or summer gas, with most of the 170 lots traded in the winter months.
January and February 1998 both gained 0.20 pence a therm p/th to 16.50 and 16.60 p/th respectively, after strong gains for first quarter gas on the over-the-counter market on Thursday.
"We saw some firm numbers on the OTC, and some of the deals were done after we closed," said one trader.
Traders said that the award of Transco's annual storage tender left many players empty handed and sent them into the market for winter gas.
Transco said on Friday that capacity at the Hornsea facility which has a direct link to the National Transmission System (NTS) was two and a half times oversubscribed.
Nevertheless prices for November and December eased lower.
"It's a real mixed bag today, it's not really clear which way it's heading," a broker said.
Transco forecast slightly stronger gas demand for Friday, at 55 percent of peak demand, but temperatures were expected to be around seasonal norms.
